text:
Alyssa: Heads-up — saw an OOM on gpu-4 around the morning spike. Looks correlated with a lot of small "mini-batches" forming while KV cache is near capacity. Flamegraph and small perf dump attached.
Ben: Can you paste the perf snippet? Is this a kernel fallback or purely memory pressure?
Alyssa: Here's the hot stack I grabbed quickly:
```
batch_assembler.cpp:assemble() +0x1f3
kv_cache.cpp:evict_loop() +0x4b
kernel_selector.cpp:fallback_to_generic() +0x98
```
Alyssa: Reproducer: run loadgen --kv_fill=0.85 --burst_ms=30 --seq_avg=512. We hit active_tokens ~3.1e6 on that GPU then OOM.
PerfBot: ALERT: OOM triggered on gpu-4 (evict loop > 5s) — incident_id=ic-20251012-42 :eyes:
Carmen: Quick hypothesis: the batch admission target (token_budget=4096) doesn't account for KV footprint. Admission admits based on in_flight tokens only, so when KV footprint spikes we oversubscribe.
Ben: Agreed. We should compute available_tokens = gpu_token_capacity - kv_reserved_tokens - in_flight_tokens * safety_factor and use that for admission.
Carmen: I tried a tiny change in assemble() that subtracts an estimated kv_tokens. Reduced OOM occurrences by ~80% in the canary but p95 increased ~12ms because batches shrank.
```
// naive patch
kv_est = estimate_kv_tokens(gpu_id);
if (kv_est > 0) {
  token_budget = std::max(128, token_budget - kv_est);
}
```
Ben: How cheap is estimate_kv_tokens() — can we derive from pages_used * bytes_per_token? Need something O(1).
Ravi: Also note kernel_selector fallback spikes when sequence length distribution shifts or when memory allocator fails to grant contiguous pages. If we route earlier to a 'compact' kernel variant when kv_reserved > threshold, we avoid fallback churn.
Alyssa: Good point. Two levers: reduce admission budget (avoid OOM) or route to a kernel that tolerates fragmented memory but is slower. Both have tradeoffs.
Ben: We should also expose kv_reserved_tokens as a metric and a per-route headroom gauge so ops can set alerts before OOM.
Alyssa: Plan: (1) implement kv-aware token admission in assembler (cheap estimator), (2) add metric kv_reserved_tokens + expose in console, (3) add kernel_selector telemetry for fallback counts, (4) run a safety sweep across safety_factor in {1.1,1.25,1.5}. I'll open a PR and run loadgen matrix tonight. :+1:
Carmen: Awesome. If you want, I can run perf profiles for the 3 safety factors and dump p95/p99 + OOM count.
Alyssa: Please do. Tagging results here will help pick the sweet spot between latency and reliability.
Ben: One more ask — add a debug flag to force kv_est=0/50/100% so we can simulate extremes without filling the cache.
Alyssa: Will add to the PR. Thanks everyone")
